docs.title: GECLens
docs.text:
Error-type-targeted evaluation of grammatical error correction (GEC) systems.

Overall F0.5 hides how a system handles a single kind of error. Subject–verb agreement, articles, prepositions and tense each make up only a few per cent of all edits. GECLens answers two questions for any ERRANT error type:

  1. Does the system fix these errors? Type F0.5, type-only F0.5, sentence-level detection and correction success.
  2. What does it break while trying? Over-correction on sentences the references leave unchanged.

Every measure comes with bootstrap confidence intervals and paired significance tests (approximate randomisation with Holm correction), for any number of systems. Results are written as CSV, Markdown and LaTeX tables and as figures.

GECLens builds on ERRANT for alignment and edit typing. Its edit-level scores are identical to errant_compare. This is checked in the test suite.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text:
pip install geclens            # or, from source: pip install -e .
python -m spacy download en_core_web_sm

Requirements: Python 3.9–3.12, ERRANT 3.0.2, spaCy 3.4–3.7 with en_core_web_sm, NumPy, Matplotlib and PyYAML. GECLens runs on Linux, macOS and Windows.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
cd examples/toy
geclens run config.yaml          # about 5 seconds

This scores three toy systems on 30 sentences for three error types and writes results/. The toy data were written by the GECLens authors and are released under CC0.

System Overall F0.5 Type F0.5 Type-only F0.5 Detection F1 Success Over-corr. careful 0.882 0.974 0.974 0.938 88.2% 0.0% eager 0.649 0.988 0.988 0.970 94.1% 100.0% cautious 0.312 0.417 0.417 0.211 11.8% 0.0%

eager fixes agreement errors as well as careful, but it also rewrites every correct sentence. Type-level F0.5 alone would not show this.

docs.title: Correctness
docs.text:
• Overall and per-type TP/FP/FN equal errant_compare -cat 3 (see tests/test_score.py).
  • Statistical routines are tested on known cases: identical systems give p = 1, Holm values are checked by hand, and bootstrap intervals contain the point estimate.
  • The CI runs the suite on Python 3.9–3.12.
pip install -e ".[dev]" && pytest

docs.title: Citation
docs.text:
If you use GECLens, please cite the software (see CITATION.cff):

P. Gautam, J. S. Thakur, A. Mishra. GECLens: A Python toolkit for error-type-targeted evaluation of grammatical error correction systems. Version 1.0.0, 2026. https://github.com/prakhargautam-ggits/GECLens

docs.title: Python API
docs.text:
from geclens import score_many, bootstrap_ci, compare_systems, profile_table, evaluate

scores = score_many("src.txt", "ref.m2", {"A": "a.txt", "B": "b.txt"}, selector="R:VERB:SVA")
scores["A"].metrics["type_only"]                    # {'tp':…, 'fp':…, 'fn':…, 'P':…, 'R':…, 'F0.5':…}
bootstrap_ci(scores["A"], resamples=2000)           # {'overall': (lo, hi), 'type': …, …}
compare_systems(scores, ["type_only", "overcorrection"], baseline="B")

evaluate("src.txt", "ref.m2", {"A": "a.txt", "B": "b.txt"}, selector="PREP", out_dir="results")

Main objects: TypeSelector, Subsets and build_subsets, SystemScore and score_system (.metrics, .components, .per_type), and bootstrap_ci, approx_randomisation, paired_bootstrap_ci, holm, compare_systems, profile_table, evaluate.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text:
# subsets and reference statistics
geclens subset  --ref ref.m2 --type R:VERB:SVA --out subsets.json

# scores with 95% bootstrap confidence intervals
geclens score   --src src.txt --ref ref.m2 --type DET \
                --hyp sysA=a.txt sysB=b.txt --ci 2000 --out-dir results

# paired approximate randomisation, Holm-adjusted, every system vs a baseline
geclens compare --src src.txt --ref ref.m2 --type PREP --hyp sysA=a.txt sysB=b.txt base=c.txt \
                --baseline base --measures type_only overcorrection --shuffles 10000

# system x error-type heatmap of ERRANT F0.5
geclens profile --src src.txt --ref ref.m2 --hyp a.txt b.txt c.txt --group category --top 12

# everything from one configuration file
geclens run config.yaml

Inputs: - --src: tokenised source sentences, one per line. - --ref: an ERRANT-typed reference M2 file. If you only have corrected text, create it with errant_parallel -orig src.txt -cor ref1.txt [ref2.txt ...] -out ref.m2. - --hyp: system outputs as text (one sentence per line) or as ready-made .m2 files.

Hypothesis M2 files are built once with ERRANT and cached.

docs.title: Output files
docs.text: File Content scores.csv / .md / .tex One row per system; the Markdown and LaTeX tables include 95% CIs <system>.json All measures and per-type ERRANT counts confidence_intervals.json Bootstrap intervals comparisons.md / .json Differences, paired-bootstrap CIs, p-values and Holm-adjusted p-values scatter.png Type-only F0.5 against over-correction profile.png / .json System × error-type heatmap subsets.json, reference_stats.json Subset indices and reference statistics

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
source: src.txt
reference: ref.m2
out_dir: results
selectors: [R:VERB:SVA, PREP, DET]      # one evaluation per selector
systems: {careful: careful.txt, eager: eager.txt, cautious: cautious.txt}
statistics: {bootstrap_resamples: 2000, shuffles: 10000, measures: [type_only, overcorrection], baseline: cautious, seed: 13}
profile: {group: category, top: 12}

Relative paths are resolved against the folder of the configuration file. With several selectors, each gets its own sub-folder of out_dir.

docs.title: What GECLens measures
docs.text:
For an error-type selector T (for example R:VERB:SVA):

Measure Definition overall ERRANT precision, recall and F0.5 over all edits type ERRANT P/R/F0.5 for edits of type T, for the annotator ERRANT selects per sentence (the one that maximises overall F0.5) type_only P/R/F0.5 after restricting hypothesis and reference edits to T, so the annotator choice depends on T edits only. Use it to compare systems that make different amounts of other edits. detection Sentence-level P/R/F1 for "the sentence contains a T error" success Share of T-positive sentences where every T edit of at least one annotator was produced exactly overcorrection Share of unedited reference sentences that the system changed (whitespace and quote style ignored) change_rate Share of all sentences the system changed

Subsets (geclens subset): positive (some annotator made a T edit), positive_all, unedited (no annotator made any edit), unedited_any, and other.

Error-type selectors: - an exact type (R:VERB:SVA); - a category, which matches its M/R/U variants (DET); - a pattern (R:VERB*); - a comma-separated list (PREP,DET).

docs.title: Statistics
docs.text:
• Bootstrap confidence intervals: sentences are resampled with replacement (B resamples, seeded); each measure is recomputed from the summed per-sentence components; the 2.5th and 97.5th percentiles give the unadjusted 95% interval.
  • Paired approximate randomisation: for each shuffle, the outputs of the two systems are swapped sentence by sentence with probability 0.5; the two-sided p-value is (number of shuffles with |d*| >= |d|, plus one) / (shuffles + 1).
  • Paired bootstrap interval of a difference: both systems are resampled with the same sentence indices.
  • Holm–Bonferroni: all tests run in one compare call form one family.
